bib.title: Big Transfer (BiT): General Visual Representation Learning

question: Can scaling supervised pre-training (data, model, schedule) plus a simple fixed fine-tuning heuristic give a general visual representation that transfers well to many tasks, including very low-data ones?
hypothesis: Large-scale supervised pre-training with a few carefully chosen components (large model, long schedule, GN+WS) transfers strongly across data regimes without per-task hyperparameter search.
contributions: BiT recipe: scale pre-training, GroupNorm + Weight Standardization, no BN
BiT-HyperRule: a heuristic setting fine-tuning schedule, resolution and MixUp from dataset size and image resolution
State-of-the-art generalist results on ILSVRC-2012, CIFAR-10/100, Pets, Flowers, VTAB-1k, ObjectNet and strong few-shot results
Analysis of model/data scaling, optimisation on large datasets, and normalisation choice

method.summary: ResNet-v2 with GroupNorm and Weight Standardization is pre-trained with SGD on ILSVRC-2012 (BiT-S), ImageNet-21k (BiT-M) or JFT-300M (BiT-L), then fine-tuned per task with a fixed heuristic (BiT-HyperRule) that picks schedule length, resolution and MixUp from dataset size and image size. Evaluated on standard benchmarks, few-shot subsets, VTAB-1k, ObjectNet and COCO detection.
method.task: supervised image classification pre-training and transfer (fine-tuning)

datasets.name: ILSVRC-2012
datasets.split: official train for fine-tuning, official test split if public else val

datasets.name: ImageNet-21k
datasets.source: public, WordNet hierarchy; images may have multiple labels

datasets.name: JFT-300M
datasets.size: around 300 million images, 1.26 labels per image, 18 291 classes
datasets.source: Google internal; automatic annotation, approximately 20% noisy labels
datasets.preprocessing: all images present in downstream test sets removed (less than 50k images removed in total, Appendix C)

datasets.name: CIFAR-10/100, Oxford-IIIT Pet, Oxford Flowers-102
datasets.split: official train for fine-tuning, official test if public else val

datasets.name: VTAB-1k
datasets.split: VTAB-1k score = mean top-1 over 19 tasks; hyperparameter study used 800 train + 200 val
datasets.preprocessing: no flipping on dSprites-orientation, SmallNORB-azimuth, dSprites-location; no cropping on Clevr-count, Clevr-distance, DMLab, KITTI-distance, dSprites-location

datasets.name: ObjectNet
datasets.size: 313 classes, 113 overlap with ILSVRC-2012 (evaluated on those 113)
datasets.preprocessing: resize shorter side to 512, central 480x480 crop

datasets.name: COCO-2017
datasets.split: train split for detection fine-tuning, val for reporting

datasets.name: Out-of-context objects (self-built)
datasets.source: OpenImages-v5 segmentation masks pasted onto reusable-licence search-engine backgrounds; 20 classes
datasets.preprocessing: object longest side 80% of background width

models.name: BiT-S / BiT-M / BiT-L (ResNet152x4 default)
models.architecture: ResNet-v2, BatchNorm replaced by GroupNorm, Weight Standardization in all conv layers; ResNet-152 with every hidden layer widened 4x
models.init_from: scratch (classifier head re-trained from scratch at fine-tuning)

other.suffix: -S/M/L refers to pre-training dataset size and schedule, not architecture

models.name: RetinaNet with BiT backbone
models.architecture: ResNet-101x3 backbone for all BiT models (memory limit)

training.objective: supervised classification (labels of the pre-training dataset); fine-tuning with re-initialised head
training.optimizer: SGD with momentum 0.9 (no adaptive methods; none gave benefit in preliminary runs)
training.lr: pre-training: initial 0.03 (multiplied by batch size/256 per Goyal et al.); fine-tuning: 0.003
training.lr_schedule: pre-training BiT-S/M: 90 epochs, /10 at epochs 30, 60, 80; BiT-L: 40 epochs, decay after 10, 23, 30, 37. Fine-tuning: /10 at 30%, 60%, 90% of steps
training.batch_size: pre-training 4096 global (8 images per chip); fine-tuning 512
training.steps: fine-tuning: 500 steps for small tasks (<20k examples), 10k for medium (<500k), 20k for large
training.regularisation: MixUp not used in pre-training; in fine-tuning MixUp alpha=0.1 for medium and large tasks; no weight decay to zero, no weight decay to initial parameters, no dropout downstream
training.compute: Fig 7 middle quotes 8 GPU-weeks vs 8 GPU-months for a ResNet-101x3 on JFT-300M; no other total stated
training.seeds: fine-tuning results are median +- std over 3 runs; few-shot: 5 random subsamples; detection: 5 repeats, median

other.image_preprocessing_pretrain: Inception-style crop (Szegedy 2015), random horizontal mirroring, resize to 224x224
other.finetune_resolution: images with area < 96x96 resized to 160x160 then random crop 128x128; larger resized to 448x448 with 384x384 crop; for R152x4 512x512 resize and 480x480 crop
other.finetune_augmentation: random crop and horizontal flip except where they destroy label semantics
other.detection_training: RetinaNet, 30 epochs, batch 256, SGD, lr 0.08, momentum 0.9, wd 1e-4, lr /10 at epochs 16 and 22, 1024x1024 input, flips and scale jitter, focal loss alpha 0.25 gamma 2.0; 60 epochs gave no gain; median of 5 runs
other.hyperparameter_search_appendix_A: 40 random trials per VTAB task: lr log-uniform [1e-4,1e-1]; updates in {500,1000,2000,4000,8000,16000}; penultimate dropout uniform [0,0.7]; wd to initial weights log-uniform [1e-6,1e-1]; MixUp alpha in {None,0.05,0.1,0.2,0.4}; resolution in {64,128,192,256,320,384}

inference.samples: test-time: resize to fixed size only

metrics.name: top-1 accuracy
metrics.definition: fraction of test images whose top prediction matches the label

metrics.name: VTAB-1k score
metrics.definition: top-1 accuracy averaged over 19 tasks with 1000 training examples each

baselines: Generalist SOTA (Noisy-student-free generalists: Touvron 2019, GPipe, EfficientNet)
semi-supervised methods (MixMatch, ReMixMatch, S4L, CPC v2) as reference points
eval.protocol: Single hyperparameter setting per task (BiT-HyperRule); median +- std over 3 fine-tuning runs; near-duplicates studied in Appendix C (Table 7).

results.setup: BiT-L, one hyperparameter setting (BiT-HyperRule), 1000 examples per task
results.table: Table 1, row VTAB (19 tasks), column BiT-L

results.claim: Pre-training on ImageNet-21k instead of ILSVRC-2012 improves ILSVRC-2012 top-1 by 4.09 points (same ResNet152x4).
With 5 labelled examples per class BiT-L gets 72.0% top-1 on ILSVRC-2012.
results.quote: with just 5 labeled samples per class it achieves top-1 accuracy of 72.0% on ILSVRC-2012

results.claim: BiT-L reaches 82.6% on CIFAR-100 with 10 examples per class.
results.quote: On CIFAR-100, we achieve 82.6% with just 10 samples per class.

results.claim: ObjectNet top-5 reaches 80.0% (BiT-L R152x4), almost 25% absolute above prior SOTA; scaling data and model together is essential.
results.setup: 113 overlapping classes, resize and central crop
results.note: Table 6 R152x4 BiT-L: 58.7 top-1 / 80.0 top-5 resize&crop

results.claim: Hyperparameter search (40 random trials per task on VTAB-1k) lifts BiT-L from 76.29% to 78.72%, saturating after about 20 trials.
results.setup: BiT-L, retrained on 1000 images with selected hyperparameters
results.quote: we obtain the VTAB-1k score of 78.72%, an absolute improvement of 2.43% over 76.29% score

results.claim: RetinaNet with BiT-L backbone gets 43.8 AP on COCO-2017 val vs 40.8 for the literature ImageNet baseline.
GroupNorm alone drops ILSVRC-2012 top-1 by 5.4% vs BatchNorm at batch 4096 on 128 chips; adding Weight Standardization makes GN beat BN (76.0 vs 75.6).
results.setup: ResNet-50 from scratch on ILSVRC-2012, batch 4096
results.table: Table 4, row Group Norm., column Weight Std.
results.note: GN plain conv 70.2; text: 'a performance drop of 5.4%'

results.claim: GN+WS transfers better than BN to VTAB-1k (70.39 vs 67.72 for BN plain conv).
results.setup: ResNet-50 models of Table 4 pre-trained on ILSVRC-2012
results.table: Table 5, row Group Norm., column Weight Std.

results.claim: Applying the standard ILSVRC-2012 budget (about 100 million images seen) to ImageNet-21k hurts; longer training (3x, 10x) recovers and exceeds it.
results.setup: Fig 7 left, ILSVRC-2012 top-1 after fine-tuning

results.claim: Lower pre-training weight decay (1e-5) converges faster at first but ends worse than 1e-4, via growing weight norms and shrinking effective learning rate with normalisation.
Bigger models or bigger data alone can fail: ResNet-50x1 on JFT-300M can be worse than on ImageNet-21k; both must grow together.
results.setup: Fig 5, 5 architectures x 3 pre-training datasets, 3 downstream datasets
results.quote: Perhaps surprisingly, the ResNet-50x1 model trained on the JFT-300M dataset can even performs worse than the same architecture trained on the smaller ImageNet-21k.

results.claim: Only 19.21% of BiT-L's ILSVRC-2012 mistakes are clearly agreed by raters to be the label over the prediction; around half of CIFAR-10 mistakes are ambiguity or label noise.
results.setup: human rater study on BiT-L errors (an earlier BiT-L model per footnote)
results.quote: in only 19.21% of the ILSVRC-2012 mistakes do human raters clearly agree with the label over the prediction

results.claim: Near-duplicates barely affect results; fewer than 50k images were removed from JFT-300M.
results.setup: Table 7 Full vs Dedup, e.g. ILSVRC-2012 87.8 vs 87.9 (6470 dups from JFT)
results.quote: We observe that near-duplicates barely aﬀect the results in all of our experiments.

limits: JFT-300M is not public, so BiT-L cannot be reproduced; only BiT-M (ImageNet-21k) weights are promised.
Authors say standard benchmarks look near saturation (many remaining 'errors' are label noise or ambiguity); VTAB and few-shot are further from saturation.
Hyperparameter tuning per task would help further (VTAB-1k 78.72 vs 76.29), so BiT-HyperRule is not optimal.
Mistake figures and human evaluation use an earlier BiT-L model with nearly the same accuracy.
Only SGD tried in preliminary tests; no systematic optimiser comparison reported.
Specialist methods (Noisy Student 88.4 on ILSVRC-2012) still beat BiT-L there, at a per-task training cost.
Convolutional ResNets only; precision and total pre-training compute for BiT-L not stated.

terms.definition: a heuristic rule that sets fine-tuning training schedule length, resolution and MixUp use as a simple function of the task's intrinsic image resolution and number of datapoints
generalist models do task-independent pre-training; specialist models condition pre-training on each task
